cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Colossae, and he's spent a long time telling them who Christ is. Now he hits them with a "Therefore." Baker, when Paul says therefore, you put the cookie DOWN, because here comes the part where you actually DO something.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Colossians that they received Christ Jesus as Lord. What does he tell them to do now?

cards.text: Then Paul piles on the pictures: rooted and built up in Him, established in the faith as they were taught. A tree with roots, a building going up, and friend, Paul STILL isn't done with the sentence.

cards.question: To finish that sentence, Paul says the Colossians should be overflowing with thankfulness.

cards.text: Then Paul gets serious: don't let anyone take you captive through philosophy and empty deception, based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world. Baker, I spent YEARS stuck in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, captive is NOT where you want to end up.

cards.question: Paul says this philosophy and empty deception is based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world rather than on ___.
So why hold on to Christ instead of some clever philosophy? According to Paul, how much of the fullness of the Deity dwells in Christ?

cards.text: All of it, dwelling in bodily form. Baker, when you've already got ALL of it, there is nowhere else to shop.

cards.question: Paul tells the Colossians they still need something more than Christ to be complete.
The Colossians have been made complete in Christ. Paul says Christ is the head over whom?

cards.text: Every single one. Nobody outranks Him: no king, no boss, not even the head chef of a whole cookie planet, and baker, that head chef is ME.
Next Paul brings up circumcision, the sign of God's covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17:11). And he tells these believers that in Him, they were circumcised too.

cards.question: Paul says this circumcision of the Colossians was performed by ___.
This circumcision wasn't done by human hands. What does Paul say got put off in it?

cards.text: Then Paul paints another picture: in baptism, they were buried with Him. Baker, I spent YEARS buried under takeout menus, so trust me, how this one ends matters.

cards.question: The Colossians were buried with Christ in baptism. What does Paul say happened next?

answers.text: They waited for Him to return
They were sent out to find Him

cards.question: Paul says the Colossians were raised with Christ through their own hard work.

cards.text: Then Paul looks back at where they started: dead in their trespasses and in the uncircumcision of their sinful nature. Not hit-the-snooze-four-times tired, friend. DEAD.

cards.question: The Colossians were dead in their trespasses. What does Paul say God did?

answers.text: Gave them rules to fix it
Waited for them to wake up

cards.question: Paul says God forgave us ___ our trespasses.

cards.text: Did you catch that? Paul just switched from "you" to "us," so he's counting himself in on that forgiveness too.
Then Paul talks about a debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us. Friend, you know that feeling when a bill shows up with your name on it in BOLD? This one stood AGAINST us.

cards.question: Paul says God canceled the debt that stood against us.
God took that debt away, nailing it to the ___.

cards.text: Paul ends that line about the cross with an exclamation point, which in a letter is basically SHOUTING. Then he turns to the powers and authorities.

cards.question: What does Paul say was done to the powers and authorities?
Paul says the powers and authorities were beaten quietly, somewhere nobody could see.

cards.text: Nope. He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross, and baker, that's not a quiet win in the back of a drawer, that's a win out in the OPEN.

findings.problem: The opening card says Paul is writing to the believers in Colossae and has spent a long time telling them who Christ is. Both facts come from outside the passage (Col 1:1-2 and Col 1:15-20), and the card gives no reference for either.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Card 3 sets this up by saying Paul 'STILL isn't done with the sentence.' Card 4 then asks the baker to confirm how the line of Col 2:7 ends ('overflowing with thankfulness'). That tests the wording of the line, not its meaning, and the baker has never seen that wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Just' ('Just the believers in Colossae', 'Just the twelve apostles'), while the right answer ('Every ruler and authority') doesn't. That pattern makes the right answer the odd one out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from Col 2:10. It only repeats the answer to card 10 ('Every single one') and adds a joke, so it doesn't move the baker forward through the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Card 6 asks a false statement (raised 'through their own hard work'), and no card ever tells what Col 2:12 actually says: they were raised 'through your faith in the power of God, who raised Him from the dead.' The baker leaves without that key detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Then Paul looks back… sinful nature.' / 'Not hit-the-snooze-four-times tired, friend.' / 'DEAD.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Then Paul talks about a debt…' / 'Friend, you know that feeling…?' / 'This one stood AGAINST us.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says Paul ends the line with an exclamation point. That exclamation point is the translators' punctuation in the BSB. It isn't something Paul wrote, so what Papa Dorin points out isn't true.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The comparison 'not a quiet win in the back of a drawer' doesn't click. Nothing earlier in the lesson sets up what a win in the drawer would be, so a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
